And if we could link this together with what's is on page 3 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S, this would be item number 8, "Conclusions": "The enemy keeps firing in provocation and attacking all defence lines in the zone of responsibility of the SRK. Despite the warnings by General Rose, they fired mortars and PAT on the Mrkovici sector from the area in Sarajevo city that is under Muslim control, the exclusion zone." Do you recall this incident where the Bosnian Muslims were firing from within the exclusion zone at Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about this specific incident because I'm not sure what -- where that is on the map. But in the event that Muslims did fire from the exclusion zone with weapons in contravention of the cease-fire -- of the agreement, we protested that. We spent a lot of time chasing and trying to track down fire units in the city that were doing this, that were in contravention. We protested against the Muslims. And going back to your point, we never asked for an air mission because there were no suitable targets to be found in a city. And the fact that they were firing at the Serbian positions -- if they were firing at the Serbian conflict positions, we would argue against a cease-fire violation but not at the fact they were firing at a position. If it hit a civilian non-combatant area, we protested. What the warring factions did with each other, that was not part of the UN mandate, as long as it followed the rules and the regulations, the agreements we had within the TEZ and the DMZ. And the idea of Rose's warnings are meaningless, that is not true. General Rose is a professional and he tried exceptionally hard with all parties to keep the situation under control. And he was effective.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that UNPROFOR did not have a complete idea of where all the Bosnian Muslim weapons and forces were located because -- because the majority of the time was spent keeping track of the Serb positions?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I mean, we tried to keep track of both sides and where the confrontation lines were, if -- where weapons systems were. And as I said just before, in the event where the Muslims did try to fire from outside the city -- from -- from the city -- from within the city on weapons that were in contravention of the cease-fire violation -- in contravention of the agreement, we would protest and we would try to apprehend those weapons systems. In one case it was a mortar that we were trying to get.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, in your question, you present two facts and the casual relationship. It's always better to first establish each of the facts and then consider the casual relationship, rather than to put them in one bunch of -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, let me follow up on that question and just ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that UNPROFOR did not know where all the Bosnian Muslim weapons and forces were located in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all the -- we knew where the confrontation line was. We knew where those units were. Some of the weapons systems we did not know where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would those be the weapons systems more in the interior of Sarajevo, in the depth of the territory behind the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In particular, the one that I referred to is the mortars that they moved around, we did not know where those were and we were always on the lookout for those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if you ask -- if the witness says that he didn't know the location of some weapons and then to ask him in the next question whether it was there and there, that is -- at least ambiguous, and without further clarification as to telling where it was, that he did know where it was. That is -- at least raises some confusion with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Your Honour's reacting to the witness's reference to the confrontation line, but I do see your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to turn to another topic. If we can now have number 1D451. This is the transcript from the Dragomir Milosevic proceedings, and I would like to have page 24 in e-court which should correlate to 1778 of that case's transcript. And I want to direct your attention to line 17 onwards. And here you indicated that you are aware of two incidents and a third shelling incident, whereby the Bosnian Muslim side had engaged in shooting at its own civilians in order to generate press that would be favourable to their side. I'd like to ask you about these incidents. And I think the --- for sake of efficiency, let's start first with the non-shelling incidents, as it were. Am I correct that there was an incident where some French soldiers related to the UNPROFOR Sector Sarajevo, that they had come across some Muslims filming a staged attack with children where no one was actually hurt, it was all staged, but that they were filming it and preparing to use it on TV against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of that incident --

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: Sorry. There was just a number of questions asked all at once. I wonder if that can be broken down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the witness said that he was aware of the incident. Mr. Ivetic, could you split it up. And to the extent you're interested in the details, to deal with them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, sir, what is your knowledge of this incident in regards to how the French soldiers came into this information?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, they just came across the situation. They reported it. And we would have brought it up to the Muslim authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- well, let's turn to the next page in the transcript, that's page 27 of 1D451. And if we can look at lines 13 through 19 of the same, sir. I think you will note and perhaps you already knew that but what I -- my question was actually reading back to you your testimony from the Dragomir Milosevic case which is at lines 16 through 19 of that transcript page. Apart from this information that I have now recited back to you, do you have any more specifics as to this incident that you could enlighten us with, or is that the totality of what you are able to say about this incident?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is all I can say about this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before we get to the shelling incident --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the parties --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take that such an incident would be recorded somewhere? It would be relevant for us to know what the report is. The witness apparently knows about the incident but has no further details, and if the -- to make it relevant, of course, we would need such information. I'm looking at both parties at this moment. Is there any report about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At this time I don't know. I know that the -- actually I should ask the witness. But I believe the witness testified in another case that he has not seen the video but that there was some video that was in the possession of the French soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I encourage the parties to try and find that material and see whether it gives further details. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, General, was I correct in recalling your testimony from a prior proceeding, that you had not seen this video but that you believed there was a video that was said to be in the possession of the French UNPROFOR officials?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard about it, never saw it, don't know anything more than what I've just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the second shooting incident? That is to say, not the shelling incident which we'll deal with after.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: So which shooting incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You -- you had testified on the prior page of the transcript that you were, in fact, aware of two incidents and a third shelling incident that was precipitated by the Serbs but finished off by the Bosnians, the Muslims. So we've now talked about one shooting incident. I wanted to know what was the other shooting incident that you had had in mind when you identified those incidents. Or perhaps it was an error and there's only one incident. I don't know. That's why I'm asking you, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a little -- I'm not sure. The one thing I can talk about is the shelling incident that started from the Serb side and finished on the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so we can get some more details about that shelling incident, am I correct that the second shell which came from the -- was deemed to have come from the Bosnian Muslim positions to a degree of certainty. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident started with a -- a shelling from the Serbs into the city, causing civilian casualties. And a short time thereafter, there was a second shelling in the same area. A joint investigation was conducted by the UN and the Muslim authorities, and the conclusions of that investigation demonstrated where the first rounds came from, from the Serbian side; and where the seconds set of rounds came from, which was on the Muslim side. And all of that was disclosed to the Muslim authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that the second round from the Muslim side came at a time when people had congregated at the site of the first shelling, and, thus, the casualties were increased?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a congregation of people. I'm not sure I would understand what your definition of "significantly increased." There were further casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You had indicated in an answer to a question a few moments ago that the UN tried to track down these Bosnian Serb weapons positions that were firing and to apprehend them. Did you, in fact, apprehend or confiscate any such weapons from the Bosnian Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not. We were -- we did not find those weapons systems, not from a lack of trying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, may I take it - and I'm also addressing you, Ms. Bolton - that there must be reports about these incidents, contemporaneous reports. I mean, so that the Chamber is better able to understand what is the area and how many casualties there were at that time. The Chamber again encourages the parties to find such reports and to tender them so that we have more detailed information, that we are better able to analysis what happened. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General Fraser, I guess it goes without saying but with regards to these two incidents there were no air-strikes sought by UNPROFOR on the part of NATO against the Bosnian Muslims. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No NATO air-strikes were sought for either party.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday at transcript page 5773, when talking about Exhibit P578, you identified that the reason that the Serbs were subjected to air-strikes was specified in that document. Am I correct, sir, that the press release, that P578, talked about incidents where the Bosnian Serb army opened fire on UN vehicles and personnel as being the reason for the air-strikes that occurred in September -- in -- at that time-period?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do believe it was in September of 1995; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to take a look at 1D00464, and it appears to be -- once this comes up, sir, I think you will see it appears to be dated 12 October 1994. And if you can look at the first page, sir, and tell me: Does that appear to be your initials as the originator of this memorandum?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that would be some -- those are my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, looking at paragraph 2 of the same, if you recall that the investigation revealed that it was without a doubt the BiH side that was responsible for attacking the airport on this occasion with mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the report states, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at that time the airport was where UNPROFOR was situated; is that correct? UNPROFOR had personnel and vehicles at the airport?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we look at item 3 on the same. And here it states: "This shelling clearly comes from the area controlled by General Fricket [as read] who is in opposition to the ongoing negotiations with his corps commander, General Karavelic, regarding the withdrawal of BiH troops from the DMZ. This incident occurred ten minutes following a meeting with the COS Sector Sarajevo and representatives from the Bosnian 1st Corps and Romanija Corps. It is believed that this incident was instigated by General Fikret in order to disrupt the ongoing negotiations." Sir, does this part of your memorandum comport fully and accurately and truthfully with your recollection of this incident and the findings made thereafter or the assessments?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection. Based on what I've just read, that is accurate and it would have resulted in a protest from UNPROFOR to the Muslim authorities at the corps level.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for clarity, this General Frickret, is that the same Brigadier Fikret that we discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is one and the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your honours, I would tender this document as the next available 1D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D00464 will be Exhibit D106.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objections, admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to turn to 65 ter number 1D00465 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as we wait for this, I can let you know, sir, that it is dated 22nd of November, 1994. And if it -- if we can turn to the -- strike that. Let's first look at items 1 through 3 on the first page, sir, wherein it is detailed that fire was opened multiple times upon the vehicle of the sector commander who was returning from a meeting with Bosnian Muslim authorities and his vehicle was struck. First of all, sir, do you recall this incident?

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLTON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. It seems to me my friend is paraphrasing, and if is he quoting from the document at page 2, it -- there's discussion about exchange of fire, not firing at the vehicle, which I think is a little different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are quoting from where, Mr. Ivetic? Because we are on page 1. If you're quoting from page 1, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's read it into the record. I was going to tender the document but, I mean, if we're going to split hairs let's read it. "On 22 November 1994 the sector commander was returning from a meeting with General Karavelic, Brigadier Fikret, and Dr. Muratovic in Hrasnica. As he was returning to Sarajevo with Dr. Muratovic, the sector commander's vehicles were engaged by small arms, resulting in several impacts to the two vehicles. "At approximately 2010 hours in the area of GR 845561 [sic], the three-vehicle convoy (police, sector commander Toyota, VBL) entered into an exchange of fire starting from the north to south and replied from south to north. This exchange of fire was over the roofs of the sector commander and VBL vehicles. It appeared that the firing came from very close because muzzle flashes were seen by the undersigned on the north side of the road 5 to 10 m away. "About 50 metres later, the convoy was once again engaged with three impacts hitting the sector commander's vehicle on the left side, north side of the road. The VBL was hit several times in the rear. Both vehicles were struck by small arms. There were no injuries."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, the question I had for you is, if you recall this incident: Where in three occasions the vehicle containing the sector commander was exposed to fire?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, because I was in the second vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we turn to the second page, the undersigned of this report, would, in fact, be yourself; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we look at item number 5 and the last -- the last -- I guess the last sentence of the same: "All shots appear to have originated from the BiH troops. Because of the sound which would indicate it was from a short distance. The flash seen by the author and the fact that trajectory could only have come from the BiH (see diagram)." Does this accord with your recollection of the assessment as to the -- who was involved in the shooting at this incident?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does. We were travelling through this area, and it appeared to be just a bunch of soldiers in the middle of the night. Isolated incident: Somebody fired, somebody shot back, and they started shooting at our vehicles in the middle. It was nothing more than an isolated incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document as the next available 1D exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 1D00465 will be Exhibit D107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, were there multiple other instances that you are aware of during your time-period when Muslim forces fired upon UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall of any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I can refresh your recollection, I call up 1D451, which is the Milosevic proceedings transcript of your testimony. And if we can have page 38 in the English -- 38 in the only version, I apologise. That will correlate to transcript page 1792. And, sir, if I can direct your attention from line 5 onward where you're answering the question directed to you I guess it was Judge Robinson. I can't see it on the screen right now, but it says here:

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Yes. We could tell from which side they were firing at. "To answer you and further explain, I think it was around the -- in April of 1995, a French soldier was coming back from the airport. He was shot and killed coming through the airport, and another French soldier was shot and killed by a sniper along Sniper Alley. One of those snipers was a Serbian that we determined along Sniper Alley; the other one we determined -- we ascertained was probably a Muslim sniper, and that one was at the airport." Does this refresh your recollection as to at least one other incident where there was -- there was an assessment that a Muslim sniper had shot and caused a fatality amongst an UNPROFOR member?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refreshes my memory now there were two incidents and think it was on 14 and 15th of April. On 14 one French soldier was killed. It precipitated the dispatch of the French chief of the defence staff to meet with the French authorities in Sarajevo. While a chief was en route on the 15th, another French soldier was killed and precipitated the dispatch of the minister of national defence to talk about the killing of those two soldiers, one by the Serbs and one by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to another topic. Again, I'd like to look at your 1997 statement, 1D457. And this will be page 20 in the English; page 21 in the B/C/S. And it is the second paragraph on the page. On page 20 of the English. And I'd like to ask you about this incident and let me just read it how it is recited here.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's the second from the top. "On the morning of October 6, 1994, a raid by a Bosnian army team took place on a Bosnian Serb Bivouac situated on Mount Igman. They left 17 dead as a result of the attack. Bosnian went through the DMZ to get there, in fact, over ground that Serbs had given up at the time of the February 1994 agreement. A mixed team was tasked to go and investigate. A written report was given out, the bodies were removed. We needed to show the Bosnian Serbs that the UN was taking quick action [sic] in order to calm the situation. A strong protest was issued to the 1st Corps. It read that all personnel in the DMZ must leave now. The Force Commander characterised it as a terrorist attack." First off, sir, does this selection accurately and truthfully reflect the basic facts of this incident as you know them?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does. It reflects a warring faction attacking another warring faction, which in itself would not be something that we would intervene. The fact that the one warring faction, the Muslims, came through the DMZ was a violation which we protested against the Muslims and reminded them of the agreement and their responsibilities to leave that affected area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The DMZ at issue - am I correct - that it had been handed over to the UN and there were UN personnel situated thereupon?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an area of continual dispute between both sides, as -- including the TEZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now the date for this particular incident was the 6th of October. I'd like to look at 1D00463. And if we can look at the first page of the document, first off, sir. Can you confirm for me that this is a document that you yourself signed and sent from Sarajevo to the BH command forward?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it is -- does it appear -- am I correct it's dated the 2nd of October; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And is this document -- it mentions a DMZ in item 1 on the first page. Is this the same DMZ, the same area that we had just discussed, where, several days later, this attack occurred?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. And, as I said before, this was -- these two areas were continual issues raised by the UN with both parties regarding the violation by both parties of weapons and activities inside both of these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn the page and look at items 2 and 3. It reflects here that at issue - at least in number 2 and 3 - there's only discussion about 200 soldiers from the 4th Brigade alleged Muslim legion and the police who were in violation of the TEZ and DMZ agreements and asked for them to be removed or if not -- if this was not resolved, that a press statement would be issued. Am I correct that at this time it was the Bosnian Muslim forces that were solely in this area in violation of the TEZ and the DMZ?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right that we were protesting against the Muslims, but your assertion that they were solely responsible would be a generalisation. Both parties were guilty of violations of the DMZ and TEZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were the Serb forces that were killed located within the DMZ or outside the DMZ?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this incident, they were outside of the DMZ. And the fact that the Muslims attacked them on that side was a -- an action between two warring parties. We protested the fact of how they got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did UNPROFOR ask NATO for air-strikes against the Bosnian Muslim forces for the violations of the TEZ and the DMZ agreement at this time?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not, because there's no appropriate target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document as the next exhibit number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D00463 will be Exhibit D108.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we can briefly turn to 65 ter number 1D00466.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while we wait for that, sir, I can give you an introduction again. It appears to be a memorandum and appears to be dated the 23rd of November, 1994. And I would ask when you review the first page, can you confirm that that is your initials signed as the originator of this document?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we look at item number 1 on the first page, it would seem that the Bosnian Serb army was still preoccupied with discussions on clearing of the DMZ. Is this, again, the same DMZ that we were talking about in October?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you, therefore, agree with me that this situation of the presence of armed Bosnian Muslim troops in a DMZ that was supposed to be under the control of UNPROFOR forces continued for an excess of one month? Actually, one and a half months, if it was the beginning of October.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the preoccupation of the UN to attempt to get the Muslims to comply with the agreement of the DMZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were any threats issued to the Bosnian Muslims? Or was it more of a -- of -- of the UN asking them to undertake something of their own accord?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't phrase it as taking something under their own accord. We reminded the Muslims of their obligation under the accord which they had signed up to and under the UN mandate. We kept reinforcing that point with them to the authorities at the corps, and up higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did anyone from the UN ever threaten the Bosnian Muslims with military strikes if they did not comply with the agreements that they had entered into?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was nothing that I recall of us threatening - using your term, not mine - the Muslims. And, again, appropriate targets would have to be determined, and that is something that is difficult to determine when you live and work in a city.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you if strikes were ever planned. I'm asking you a different question. Were -- was the threat of strikes ever used to try to entice the Muslim forces to abide by the agreements they had signed?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't make threats unless you are prepared to follow through with them. The UN did not make fallacious threats. We only --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is there --

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- we only protested and did concrete action that we knew we could follow through with that could achieve the desired effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just try to understand what's going on. The first question was - 66, line 17 - Did anyone from UN of threaten? I make it short. "A. There was nothing that I recalled of us threatening." So that is a no. And next question: "I'm not asking whether strikes were planned. I'm asking a different question, whether there were threat of strikes." And then that answer does not repeat the previous answer, we only protested. It's -- from the answers, I take it that the witness has told us twice that there were no threats. If there would have been threats, that you would only express threats if you would be willing to give it a follow-up; but if there's no threats, then that is superfluous to tell us, and then he told us what was going on. I do not see what's -- I mean, did I understand your answer well, that never threats were made to the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we never threatened the Muslims. We only protested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I to take your answer that the UN was not prepared to consider the option of air-strikes against the Bosnian Muslims, even for multiple and repeated violations of the cease-fire and the TEZ and DMZ agreements, even if such violations were ongoing for a period of over a month?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The UN also considered the option of air-strikes, but the decision at the time was to protest against the Muslim authorities regarding the violations of the DMZ. That was the action taken. But it was ... that -- that's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. I'm happy to move onto another topic. Yesterday at transcript page 5783 and forwards, you discussed for several pages the modified air bombs. In particular, you talked about the beaten zone for that weapon being of 500 metres and how you could not control the point of impact. First of all, sir, am I correct that you have never had any training or experience in the use of such a weapons system?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I've not had training in that weapons system, 30 years in the army, having commanded two Mortar Platoons, having commanded a brigade using rockets, missiles, aircraft, and the basic training and the continuous training that I have received, I am more than qualified to provide commentary, and my opinion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. The question was whether you had any training. I wondered what that question was about. Because I understood from your statement that it was at that moment that you for the first time learned about the existence of such a weapon. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So whether you are trained in the use of a weapon, where the statement clearly says that you only learned about the existence of it at that moment, that needs, at least, some clarification, why to ask such a question. And then you started answering, more or less defending yourself against what you considered might be an attack on your knowledge, where there was no need to do that. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, I was trying to find a bases for the evidence elicited by the Prosecution yesterday at transcript pages 5783 and onwards, where this witness said that one could not control the point of impact of such a weapon. And if he has not had any training or experience in it, I'm wondering what the bases of that conclusion is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps analysis after you have seen something, that's a possibility. But the training question really is -- well, it seems to be a routine question more or less, were you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- trained in this? Were you trained in that? That routine is not always necessary; I wanted to point that out. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you have not consulted any books or manuals about the beaten zone of that weapon or the schematics of that weapon?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not. All I have done is read the report from the artillery commander who gave the facts as to the potential beaten zone for that weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that you've never seen such a weapons system since you left Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you've not performed any analysis since leaving Bosnia about the capabilities or schematics of such a weapons system?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could call up P580. That's the document that I believe you have referenced. And with all due respect to your military experience, sir, isn't there a difference between beaten zone and the so-called lethal zone or danger zone of an indirect fire weapon?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're part and parcel of the same thing, and perhaps you could explain what you mean by "both" in your terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd prefer to direct you to Colonel John Hamill, a career artillery officer who testified in this trial at transcript page 5519 and 5520, that a 500-metre danger zone applied to a 120-millimetre mortar round. Does that sound about right to you?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's probably right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So would you agree with me, then, that one conclusion we can reach from P580 is that the modified aerial bomb has the same approximate danger zone as a 120-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that fails to take into consideration the ballistic capability of that round as it travels through the air about where it will fall within that beaten zone, and within the beaten zone the lethal radius of that round. You have to take into consideration both factors. And that's just a theoretical discussion about beaten zones and the lethal zone around the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that this document, which seems to be concerned with potential injuries or perhaps fatalities, 200 and 500 metres from the entrance of a target is only able to help us with respect to the lethal radius and the danger zone of this particular weapon?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It starts to go in that direction - I would agree with that much - but two numbers on a report just begs more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree. And you were very confident yesterday when you said this shows the beaten zone to be thus and so. Am I correct that this document does not permit us to make any qualifications as to the beaten zone of this particular weapons system?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a starting point, this document would allude to at least a beaten zone of 500 metres, and I would like to go back and check on my -- how I responded to that question -- but as a start point, at least 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have to opportunity to do that after the break, if there's any need to do it. There is a procedural matter I'd like to raise, but we don't need you for that, Mr. Fraser, so would you already follow the -- the usher. Yes, and come back after approximately 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter the Prosecution would like to raise is appropriately raised in private session or in open session, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Private session, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll take a break and resume at quarter past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic, could you give us a further impression as to how much time you would need, assuming that you would use the next 15 minutes today?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd need probably another 15 minutes, because I have about half an hour left, which was the original estimate of four hours, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Fraser, could I first ask your attention. There may be some text on the screen. I'd invite you not to read it because that was part of private session and it's not relevant for your testimony, and it's even confidential. So if you would not start reading the screen until -- if I talk for another five minutes then we would be there, but I will refrain from doing that. Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, I'd like to ask you now with respect to this modified aerial bomb, first of all, we're talking about a 250-kilogramme bomb. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that a 250-kilogramme bomb landing on a concrete or brick building might punch a hole in it but would be little or no damage?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that landing on the ground it would have a greater impact in the sense of sending up shrapnel and fragments but that the radius would depend on whatever size the warhead contained in the bomb is?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And be a function of the type of ground it landed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to this weapons system, do you agree that if tested and fired and analysed, the performances of the weapons system can be determined and a firing table for the same can be established?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If all those conditions were met, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as you sit here today, you do not have access to any firing tables or analyses of any such test to assume that all those conditions were met or not?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not. The only thing I have is that one report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'd like to now to discuss an area that you spent considerable time on in your statement, proportionality, and I would like to explore some issues relative to the same. First of all, on this issue of proportionality of a military action, have you authored any articles, books, or treatises on this specific topic?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not authored, lectured.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. How many lectures?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, other than what I've taught at the Army Staff College and the Canadian Forces College in Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Have you ever served as an expert witness in any legal proceeding, including court-martial proceedings, on the topic of whether a particular military action was proportionate or disproportionate?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but your position is based primarily on what you understand the Canadian military doctrine or standards of proportionality to be?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The basis is Canadian but within the context of operating within a coalition, that coalition be it the UN or another coalition like NATO. Each and every one of us who wears a uniform is based in that particular country; but based on how operations are done normally as a part of a bigger team, we have to make sure that we take what we come with and are able to apply and work together to achieve desired effects.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You've brought up coalition within either NATO or the UN. In regard to the situation in Bosnia during the time-period that you were there, when military air-strikes were sought against a party - we'll leave it general for now, although I understand your testimony that it was not ever sought against the Muslims - but in the instances when it was sought, who would select the targets for the air-strikes that were to be carried out? Would it be the United Nations? UNPROFOR? NATO? Or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would start off with the UN determining a target, and then there would be a dialogue between the UN, the recommending authority, and the NATO to determine the suitability of platform and target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we can return to the Canadian military perspective, am I correct that part of the analysis of a proportionate military action involves attempting to minimise the cost or expenditure of the ordnance of munitions to achieve a particular military objective?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand, you're talking about collateral damage?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just re --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about in terms of proportionality of a military fire mission. Is part of the analysis also, in terms of choosing which ordnance or weapon to use, take into account an effort to minimise the cost expenditures to use the minimum ordnance necessary to achieve a military objective for a fire mission?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not cost expenditures but the weapon versus the target. So if I can give an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To -- if you have a sniper that you want to take out, using a -- I'm -- just for illustrative purposes, a thousand-pound bomb would be disproportional for the sniper. The ideal weapons system to take out a sniper would be another sniper; that would be proportional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think Mr. Ivetic did put a different question to you. Could I, first of all, see whether I understood the question by rephrasing it. If you would choose a weapon in a proportionate attack, would you sometimes choose perhaps a weapon stronger than really needed for that attack because it would be cheaper? Is that more or less -- cheaper in terms of ... if this is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's not -- that's actually a twist I had not thought of, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, please -- then apparently the question at least was not clear to me. Rephrase it in such a way what you mean by "expenditure" in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will try to do that by focussing on what the witness just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You said that the ideal weapons system would be another sniper. Is that, in terms of the -- the costs of having a sniper as opposed to some other ordnance, let's say, a mortar? Is that part of the analysis within the Canadian tradition, military tradition?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the terminology that you use, "cost." We don't -- I just don't understand when you say "cost," are you talking about a monetary cost? Are you talking about a figurative cost of -- I just don't quite understand when you use the word "cost." When I say "proportionality" - and this is not just Canadian, it is -- it is common amongst the militaries that I have dealt and what is taught - is you try to match the target with a system that can actually deal with the effect that you want to achieve vis-a-vis that target. Sniper -- to take out a sniper, you use another sniper. If you have a tank, ideally you probably want to use another tank to take out that tank, if it was available.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this in your hypothetical of a sniper. What -- if the ideal weapons system is not available, is it still legitimate to use another weapons system to eliminate that military objective, can it be?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You then have to weigh escalating the weapons system that is available against the target that you're trying to achieve that effect. And you may get to a point in that analysis of proportionality where the costs of achieving the desired effect become not sustainable, not supportable. That was only one factor in amongst a number of factors when you talk about a target and what you want to achieve with that target. Hence, earlier, I said "collateral," which is another factor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Would you agree with me that there were Bosnian Muslim military units scattered throughout Sarajevo and that the Muslims sometimes purposely intermixed them with civilian areas -- mixed them into civilian areas?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that it is an obligation of an army or armed force to distinguish its soldiers and place insignia or markings on the uniforms to differentiate them from civilians?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Bosnian Muslim armed forces in Sarajevo, in large part, did not wear proper uniforms but often had civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I could agree with that statement completely because I don't have -- I don't have enough information that would suggest the latter, i.e., that they -- you said "often had civilian clothing." I don't have a lot of information that would support that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Did you witness members of the Bosnian Muslim armed forces performing their duties while wearing civilian clothing or at least clothing without identifiable emblem or insignia?

utterances.speaker: DAVID FRASER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm looking at the clock. We're one and a half minutes from --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then we should probably pull the plug here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Fraser, we'd like to see you back tomorrow. We'll start at 9.30 in this -- not in same courtroom but in Courtroom III. We'd like to see you back. You may follow the usher. And I, again, instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in any other way about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Friday, the 7th of December, at 9.30 in the morning, in Courtroom III.
